messages:
sara: quick heads-up - we started seeing a batch of 403s from ingest-worker when it talks to legacy-ingress. the error is 'missing org claim' even though the token is project-scoped. any quick wins?

josh: which route is failing? example log?

sara: pasted a sanitized trace:
```
2026-03-22T14:02:11Z ingest-worker->legacy-ingress 403 missing org claim token=proj:abcd1234
route=/v1/push
headers: Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
```

mike: legacy-ingress expects an org-level header (x-org). project-scoped tokens don't include org by design. options: 1) translate at ingress (inject x-org), 2) mint a short-lived org-scoped token (broker), 3) change downstream to accept project tokens (big).

elaine: tradeoffs: translate is low-friction but hides the original principal unless we forward raw claims. minting gives clearer audit but requires broker perms & KMS ops. altering downstream is long runway.

auth-bot: Incident 3242: recurring 403s from svc ingest-worker - 18 hits in 10m.

josh: my prefered pattern: lightweight claim-normalizer sidecar on the legacy-ingress pod. it would: (a) look for org claim, (b) if missing, lookup(project_id) -> org_id, (c) set x-org header only for routes in allowlist, and (d) attach x-auth-raw to preserve provenance. no token exchange, no new KMS ops.

mike: +1 but ensure least-privilege: sidecar must have read-only access to project->org mapping and no long-term token storage. also limit header injection to specific paths via config:
```
allowlist:
  - /v1/push
  - /v1/legacy/*
```

elaine: two concerns: (1) audit: downstream will see x-auth-raw - we should hash the raw token or attach a trace id instead of full token, (2) impersonation risk: if someone can set x-auth-raw upstream, we need to drop incoming x-org/x-auth-raw before normalization.

josh: agree. implement normalization as:
```
# pseudocode
if not token.claims.org:
  org = lookup_org_from_project(token.claims.project)
  set_header('x-org', org)
  set_header('x-auth-trace', hash(token.raw)[:16])
else:
  pass
# drop any incoming x-org/x-auth-trace before doing this
```

sara: rollout plan proposal: canary at 5% of ingress pods for 24h, metric auth_403_legacy -> expect reduction. add alert if auth_403_legacy spikes or auth_normalize_errors > 0.

mike: test matrix: unit tests for mapping, e2e with a fake legacy-ingress, plus RBAC smoke where project mapping returns null -> should 403 (no silent panic).

elaine: ops: add an audit sink entry with schema {trace, projected_org, project_id, normalized_by}. ensure logs redact token but keep hashed trace.

josh: i'll draft a minimal PR for the sidecar and a small operator flag: --normalize-claims=true and --normalize-allowlist=/etc/normalize/allowlist.yaml

sara: can you also include a compatibility-mode where service can opt-out with header x-allow-normalize: no ? we might need this for some customers.
josh: sure. sidecar will respect incoming x-allow-normalize when set to 'no' and caller has admin role (easy guard).

elaine: open questions for RFC: whether project->org mapping is read from cached config (fast) vs call to central directory (strongly consistent). recommend cache + TTL 5m and fallback to sync call on miss.

mike: perf note: single lookup per unique project per TTL. attach metrics: normalize_lookup_miss_rate, normalize_latency_ms.

auth-bot: created ticket #SE-875: 'claim-normalizer sidecar for legacy-ingress'.

sara: action items: (1) josh open PR + demo, (2) mike add tests & perf metrics, (3) elaine write RFC note with audit schema and threat model. i'll own canary config and monitor dashboards.

josh: tagging owners: @mike @elaine will sync tomorrow 10am. thanks :thumbsup:
